business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bulk Vessel Brokerage of Agricultural Soybeans and Yellow Corn

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Ley 11/2021, de 9 de julio; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, approving the Regulation of Law 10/2010; Real Decreto 280/2021, de 27 de abril, developing the Central Registry of Beneficial Ownership (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales); Directive (UE) 2018/843 (AMLD5) transposed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Legal Existence or Good Standing of the corporate shareholder (or notarized passport copy for a direct individual shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial/Companies Registry in shareholder’s jurisdiction; Spanish notary if directly executed before him

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder) authorising the Spanish incorporation agent and attorneys
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in shareholder’s jurisdiction or Spanish notary for execution in Spain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization if issuer is outside the Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statutory audit report or financial statements of the corporate shareholder (last fiscal year, if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered auditor or regulatory body in shareholder’s country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter indicating provenance of funds for the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Hague Apostille; Consular Legalization if origin is a non-Hague country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of tax residence of the shareholder or of absence of Spanish tax residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax authority of the shareholder’s country

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders holding more than 25%, UBOs and authorised signatories are screened against: (i) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) EU Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) listing; (iii) US OFAC SDN List; (iv) Spanish SEPBLAC internal lists; and (v) FATF high-risk and non-cooperative jurisdictions. PEP status is verified using commercial-list screening and self-declaration, applying FATF Recommendations 12 and 22. Enhanced due diligence is imposed where a PEP is identified or where funds originate from a high-risk jurisdiction listed by the EU.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) electronic application – https://www.rmc.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Consolidated Text of the Capital Companies Act (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010) and the Mercantile Registry Regulation (Real Decreto 1784/1996), a company name must be unique, verboten to be contrary to law, morality or public order, and may be expressed in Spanish or in any official language of an Autonomous Community. Latin script is mandatory with standard Spanish transliteration for foreign names. Foreign terms are allowed only if not descriptive and if transliterated accurately. The abbreviation 'S.L.' or 'S.R.L.' must be used in line with the chosen form.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Sociedad Anónima (when not the correct public limited form)
Cooperativa (when not the correct cooperative form)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RMC denies the proposed name, the applicant receives a reasoned denial. The applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within one month from notification under Articles 121 and 122 of the Ley 39/2015. Alternatively, the applicant may resubmit a new name application with up to three preferred alternatives ranked in priority order. In exceptional cases, an extension of the reservation is not automatic; the applicant must re-file a fresh name request after the expiration of the 90-day validity period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office (domicilio social) is permissible for an SL at initial incorporation, provided that a physical Spanish postal address capable of receiving official notifications is contracted from a licensed virtual-office provider. For this specific bulk grain and soybean/corn brokerage activity (ISIC 4631), the tax authorities rarely dispute a virtual office at formation, but an office able to perform occasional customer meetings or document retention is recommended to demonstrate commercial substance if VAT registration or tender participation is requested.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: 5%–10% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months. The risk is higher if the company registers a virtual address that is shared by multiple unrelated entities in a known post-restante structure, or if the tax authority receives inconsistent declarations from the legal representatives.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance certificate (Certificación de Denominación Social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Mercantile Registry Regulation)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary fees for incorporation deed (Escritura de Constitución)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary designated by the incorporators (Colegio Notarial transaction)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff regulated by the Ministry of Justice, calculated on share capital and deed pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil de la provincia del domicilio social
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registration fee based on nominal or assigned capital under the legal tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel and gestoría incorporation filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Spanish market benchmark for foreign-owned SL formation (€700–€900)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO/KYC/AML screening and compliance file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for electronic screening against UN, EU, OFAC and SEPBLAC lists plus document validation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign shareholder documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or consulate of shareholders' jurisdictions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official public tariff plus courier/priority service benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation service (virtual office with physical receipt)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Domiciliation service provider with a valid Spanish address
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual contract for Madrid or Barcelona virtual office (€45–€60 per month) plus setup fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Application for provisional NIF (CIF) and definitive NIF after incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) via gestoría
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: AEAT filing is without public fee; gestoría handling charge for tax ID process

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio): Articles 4 (minimum share capital), 20-23 (incorporation requirements and public deed), 24 (subscribed capital and payment), 62 (registered office), and 113-140 (administration). Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil) governs registration, and Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1993 (ITP-AJD) covers stamp duty.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (for name reservation) and Registro Mercantil Provincial de Madrid (for inscription of the incorporation deed).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (notarial deed of incorporation) and subsequent inscripción en el Registro Mercantil.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Standard SL minimum capital is EUR 3,000 (Art. 4 LSC), fully subscribed and paid up in cash at constitution. The capital must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution account opened in the company's name or deposited with the Notary as cash, evidenced by a certificación bancaria de depósito with restricted release until registry inscription. Alternative: Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva (Ley 18/2022) permits EUR 1 capital with restrictions on profit distribution until the EUR 3,000 threshold is reached.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST: That the share capital, fixed at EUR 3,000, divided into 3,000 equal participations of EUR 1.00 each, is approved, fully subscribed and paid up, and the allotment to the founding shareholders is ratified. RESOLVED SECOND: That the registered office is adopted at Calle Ejemplo 12, 28001 Madrid, Spain, constituting the legal seat, tax address, and Commercial Registry venue. RESOLVED THIRD: That [Full Name] is appointed Sole Administrator with the broadest powers by law, including executing the incorporation deed, filing registry applications, opening bank accounts, and obtaining all licenses. RESOLVED FOURTH: That the Sole Administrator may retain legal counsel and notaries as necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Corporate Name (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC), Madrid - online application portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application to the Registro Mercantil Central proposing three corporate names in descending preference order. The RMC verifies the proposed names against the central index of existing companies and issues the negative certification reserving the chosen name exclusively for three months. Attach the founders' identity documents and manually sign the application if required.
required_dossiers: Passport or NIE of each founding shareholder
Three proposed company names in order of preference
Official application form for negative name certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, file a new application with substitute names. The certificate may be renewed or extended by re-application within the validity period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF Provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Delegación de Madrid, form 036
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file Modelo 036 for the provisional NIF, attaching the negative name certificate and appointing a tax representative resident in Spain. State the intended Spanish tax address of the company. The AEAT verifies the census data and issues the provisional NIF, which must be quoted in the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Modelo 036 (censo de personas jurídicas)
Certificación negativa de denominación social
NIE or passport of each incorporator
Proof of intended Spanish registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT issues a requerimiento, correct the stated census data and resubmit the declaration within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Capital Escrow and Bank Deposit Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Spanish credit institution or the Notary Public directly
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an incorporation account in the company's proposed name and deposit the minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, or alternatively deliver the capital sum in cash to the notary. Obtain from the bank an original certificación bancaria de depósito identifying the depositor, the company name, and the restricted-availability clause prohibiting release until the company is registered in the Commercial Registry.
required_dossiers: Provisional NIF of the company to be formed
Negative name certification
Passport or NIE of subscribing shareholders
Written instruction to the bank for the restricted escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank certificate omits the restricted release clause, request a supplementary confirmation letter from the branch manager before proceeding to notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Incorporation Deed (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notario) selected by the founders, Madrid
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding shareholders or their duly authorized attorneys must appear personally before the notary, present the negative name certificate, provisional NIF, capital deposit certificate, and executed draft bylaws. The notary verifies the legality of the articles, reads the deed and statutes, confirms the paid-up capital, and issues the copia autorizada (certified copy) for registry filing. Foreign shareholders must present apostilled passport copies and, where required, NIE numbers.
required_dossiers: Certificación negativa de denominación social
Provisional NIF (Modelo 036 confirmation)
Bank capital deposit certificate or notarial receipt of paid-up capital
Signed draft bylaws (estatutos sociales)
Passport or NIE of each shareholder, apostilled if foreign
Identification and acceptance of the appointed Sole Administrator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial refusal only occurs in case of unlawful corporate purpose or defective capital payment; cure by rectifying the bylaws or perfecting the capital deposit and reappearing before the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Commercial Registry (Inscripción en el Registro Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the certified copy of the deed (copia autorizada) and the second original copy (testimonio) with the commercial registry within one month of notarization. The registrar examines the legality of the deed and the capital rules (calificación registral) and, upon approval, enters the company in the registry, at which point the SL acquires full legal personality. Evidence of the ITP-AJD stamp duty payment must accompany the filing.
required_dossiers: Certified notarial deed (copia autorizada)
Second original deed copy (testimonio) for the registry file
Updated Modelo 036 census confirmation
Self-assessment of ITP-AJD stamp duty (Modelo 600)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues suspension or denial (calificación desfavorable), obtain a notarial rectification deed to correct the defect, or file a written response with supplementary documentation within the statutory cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining definitive NIF and Commencement of Tax and Municipal Activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and Ayuntamiento de Madrid - Ventanilla Única Empresarial
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, file the final Modelo 036 to convert the provisional NIF into a definitive NIF within 15 days, quoting the registry inscription data. Then submit the municipal declaración responsable de inicio de actividad under Ley 12/2012, register for the IAE under epigraph 616 (wholesale trade of foodstuffs and agricultural products), and, if premises are leased, attach the landlord's consent or occupancy certificate.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry inscription certificate or registered copy of the deed
Definitive NIF application (Modelo 036)
Company deed and identification of the legal representative
Lease agreement or proof of ownership of the business premises
Landlord's consent for the declared activity and occupancy certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late communication of activity may trigger municipal sanctions and IAE surcharges; cure by filing the omitted declaration with a written explanation and, where available, a surcharge exemption request within one month of detection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General de Industria, Energía y Minas (Autonomous Community of Madrid) for industrial premises; Ayuntamiento de Madrid - Departamento de Licencias for municipal activity and urban planning clearance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating license is mandated for pure wholesale grain and oilseed brokerage activity. A municipal declaración responsable de inicio de actividad under Ley 12/2012, together with IAE epigraph 616 registration, is required. If the company later operates dedicated grain silos or warehouses, a Licencia Urbanística y de Actividad (Licencia de Apertura) will be required from the municipality.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental - Consejería de Medio Ambiente de la Comunidad de Madrid; Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Pure wholesale brokerage is not listed in Annexes I or II of Ley 21/2013 on environmental assessment. If ancillary silo or warehouse storage of grain is introduced, the activity enters the regional Comunicación Ambiental category and may require a compliance assessment depending on storage capacity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source discharges arise from office brokerage activity. For any future grain handling or silo operation, comply with Royal Decree 102/2011 (PM10 and dust limits), ATEX Directive 2014/34/EU on explosive dust atmospheres, Ley 7/2022 on waste and contaminated soils, and Royal Decree 1367/2007 on noise. Any industrial wastewater discharge, if introduced, must meet Royal Decree 817/2015 quality thresholds for water bodies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety compliance is required under Royal Decree 513/2017 (regulations for fire safety installations in industrial establishments), evidenced by a certificado de protección contra incendios and the municipal opening license. The office or warehouse premises must hold an occupancy certificate (licencia de primera ocupación) verifying structural load limits. The company must adopt an occupational risk prevention plan, conduct workplace risk assessments, and complete emergency training under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales. If port-based bulk handling is later added, port facility security authorization under the ISPS Code and approval of the relevant Port Authority will be mandatory.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Ministry of Finance and Public Function — electronic portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spain issues NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) to resident companies and to non-resident entities acting through a Spanish branch or PE. For the Spanish SL: (1) obtain provisional B-prefix NIF via Form 036 before executing the notarial deed; (2) register the deed at the local Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) within one month of incorporation; (3) present the Registry certificate to AEAT to convert the provisional NIF into a definitive NIF and to inscribe the company in the Censo de Empresarios. The same census filing registers the SL for VAT (IVA), Corporate Income Tax (IS), and withholding-agent positions. A non-resident foreign entity without a PE that invoices Spanish customers or applies for VAT refunds must appoint a tax representative (representante fiscal) and file Form 036 (Form 030 for individuals); a specific NIF for non-residents is then issued. No separate sectoral license is required for wholesale grain brokerage, but the company should file the annual statistical operations declaration (Contabilidad anual and Modelo 200) once operative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SL is a resident taxpayer for Spain's Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014, general rate 25%) and is taxed on worldwide income. No default pass-through treatment exists for an ordinary commercial SL; the UTE/AIE transparent vehicles are exceptional alternatives outside the chosen structure. The territorial scope normally follows worldwide taxation with foreign tax credit, and Spain applies CFC rules plus ATAD anti-hybrid provisions without elective carve-outs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' or U.S.-style pass-through election is available for an SL. Optional regimes and elections that can be invoked: (i) 15% reduced CIT rate for newly created small entities in their first two profitable years (maximum taxable base €300,000); (ii) 23% reduced tranche for the first EUR 50,000 of taxable base for entities with turnover under EUR 1,000,000; (iii) tax consolidation (grupo fiscal) election under arts. 61–78 LIS for groups with ≥70% direct or indirect shareholding; (iv) ETVE holding-company regime under arts. 21 and 100 LIS for full exemption of qualifying dividends and capital gains; (v) special VAT grouping (grupo de IVA) for consolidation; (vi) accrual vs. cash-based invoicing elections under special regimes where applicable. Hybrid-mismatch elections are disallowed and permanently firewalled by transposed ATAD provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Ley 37/1992, Royal Decrees 1624/1992 and 1619/2012)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold exists for trading companies in Spain; any economically active entity must be VAT-registered (Form 036, Censo de Empresarios) before commencing activity. Optional simplified regimes (Régimen Simplificado, applicable to small retail/trader entities) are not recommendable for B2B commodity brokerage and are excluded by the SL's corporate form and client base. The mandatory SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) regime applies to taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000, to those in consolidated VAT groups, and to those invoicing under large-company declarations; SII obligors must transmit each invoice and relevant refund record to AEAT within four working days.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not operate a centralized real-time clearance system of the Italian SDI type; the SII regime approximates near-real-time control by requiring booking-level XML/JSON submission via the AEAT web service or REST API within 4 working days from issuance or reception. Regulatory reform under Ley Crea y Crece (Ley 28/2022) and Royal Decree 1007/2023 ('Verifactu') mandates: (i) interoperable B2B electronic invoicing using facturae XML 3.2 or equivalent standards; and (ii) certified billing software that generates an integrity Hash + QR code per invoice and preserves a tamper-evident electronic register with a digital stamping record. Compliance deadlines for the private-sector mandate are being phased between 2024 and 2026 depending on company turnover, pending the final implementing regulation; until then, SII is the only mandatory near-real-time channel.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Bulk physical supplies of soybeans and yellow corn exported from Spain to non-EU ports qualify for the export exemption with right of deduction (effectively 0%) under art. 21(1) Ley 37/1992, provided that (i) the buyer is established outside the EU; (ii) the goods physically leave the EU customs territory within 90 days of the start of dispatch; and (iii) the exporter holds full documentary proof of exit (DUA validated by Customs, bill of lading, port of loading evidence). The brokerage or commission element of the ISIC 4631 activity follows separate place-of-supply rules: if the customer is a non-EU established trader, the service falls outside Spanish VAT (not subject, art. 70 LIVA); if the customer is an EU/Spanish counterparty, the intermediation in the sale of goods is subject to Spanish 21% VAT or to the reverse-charge mechanism (art. 84.uno.2.a LIVA). The invoice must unambiguously segregate the goods supply (0%) from the brokerage fee (0% not-subject or 21%) to avoid full re-characterization.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Official Customs Export Declaration (DUA — Documento Único Administrativo / SAD) with electronic validation through the Export Control System (ECS/AES)
Bill of Lading (or equivalent ocean transport document) evidencing physical departure from an EU port

Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT wire evidence of settlement of export proceeds (anti-money-laundering verification and banking due diligence; Spain imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation obligation)
Commercial invoice with FOB price, INCOTERMS, and commodity specification
Certificate of Origin (EUR.1 or importer-declared) and phytosanitary/ health certification for bulk grains
Packing list, weight certificate / draft survey report, and marine insurance certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The 0% export exemption is retrospectively clawed back if the exporter cannot prove physical departure within 90 days of dispatch (art. 22 LIVA): AEAT will assess the invoiced amount plus 21% VAT, accrued late-payment interest, and a penalty surcharge of 50% to 150% of the tax base under arts. 170–171 Ley General Tributaria. Where false DUA/BL documentation or fictitious exports are used to claim refunds (MTIC-pattern fraud), criminal liability applies under art. 305 Código Penal (fines up to six times the defrauded amount and imprisonment of 1 to 5 years). Retroactive clawback may extend four fiscal years from the filing date, and the statute of limitations for fraudulent schemes is prolonged. Documents must be retained at least 10 years. For the brokerage component, AEAT actively recharacterizes disguised sales commissions as taxable services where invoices are not clearly split; such recharacterization triggers 21% VAT, penalty, and submission to the special large-debtors file. Export refund claims (Modelo 303/390 with SII) are subject to enhanced scrutiny, and any mismatch between customs declarations and VAT accounts is automatically flagged by AEAT's cross-checking system (Data Warehouse / verificación de datos).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, acting within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange and capital-movement matters are also subject to the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise and its General Directorate of the Treasury and Financial Policy. Applicable EU authorities and rules include the European Central Bank, the European Commission, the European Banking Authority, EU sanctions regulations, the EU Anti-Money Laundering framework, the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, and the Single Euro Payments Area framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro, which is freely convertible for ordinary commercial and financial transactions. Current-account payments, including payments for imported agricultural commodities, freight, brokerage, insurance, services, dividends, interest, and trade receivables, are generally transferable without exchange-control approval. Capital movements are also generally free within the EU legal framework, including foreign direct investment, shareholder loans, intercompany funding, acquisition proceeds, and repatriation of profits. Restrictions may arise from sanctions, anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist-financing controls, cash limitations, national-security investment screening, prudential bank controls, tax compliance, and documentary requirements imposed by the servicing bank. Dividend distributions require distributable accounting profits, satisfaction of Spanish corporate-law solvency and reserve requirements, appropriate shareholder approval, and withholding-tax analysis. Interest, royalties, service fees, and related-party payments require arm's-length support, beneficial-owner verification, transfer-pricing documentation, and applicable withholding-tax and treaty analysis. Non-EU shareholders may also be subject to foreign-investment reporting or screening depending on the investor, sector, transaction structure, and applicable national-security rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement for exporters to surrender export proceeds to a domestic bank and no general mandatory conversion ratio or statutory deadline requiring conversion of foreign-currency export receipts into euros. The company may retain eligible foreign-currency balances with an authorised bank, subject to the bank's account terms, accounting rules, tax reporting, sanctions controls, and transaction-monitoring requirements. Export proceeds must be supported by commercial documentation, including contracts, invoices, transport documents, customs or Intrastat evidence where applicable, and evidence of delivery or performance. Banks may request payment-purpose information, counterparty data, customs references, and source-of-funds evidence. Residents may have statistical or regulatory reporting obligations for certain external assets, liabilities, or payment transactions, depending on applicable thresholds and reporting rules. Cash transactions are subject to Spanish legal limits, and cash exports or imports of EUR 10,000 or more, or the applicable equivalent, generally trigger declaration requirements when entering or leaving the EU.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment collection, multicurrency wallets, supplier payments, and euro SEPA transfers; low as a substitute for a full-service Spanish corporate bank for capital registration, trade finance, documentary letters of credit, commodity-related enhanced due diligence, and complex third-country flows. An electronic money institution or payment institution authorised in the EU may passport services into Spain, but it is not a bank, normally does not provide ordinary deposit-taking, and may safeguard rather than deposit customer funds. Offshore digital EMIs without EU authorisation, passporting, or a compliant local programme should not be used for regulated payment services in Spain. The company must verify the provider's authorisation in the relevant EU register, legal entity, safeguarding model, funds availability, sanctions policy, transaction limits, data-access rights, and termination procedures. EMI onboarding does not eliminate Spanish tax, AML, beneficial-ownership, sanctions, customs, or transfer-pricing obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not generally require every director to appear physically at a bank branch for corporate-account opening. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the bank accepts qualified electronic identification, video identification, certified documents, and a satisfactory non-face-to-face customer-due-diligence process. In practice, banks may require an in-person meeting or live video interview for a newly incorporated SL, non-resident ownership, foreign directors, complex ownership chains, commodity trading, high-risk jurisdictions, unusual payment corridors, or trade-finance facilities. The company should appoint a Spain-based authorised signatory or treasury contact where commercially practical and maintain Spanish-language or certified translations of corporate documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner, particularly where the ownership chain includes multiple holding entities or nominee arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles of association; notarial deed and Registro Mercantil extract; complete ownership chart to each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; passports and proof of address; tax-identification numbers; director and signatory resolutions; powers of attorney; certified translations where requested; and written explanation of the ownership, control, and economic rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commodity trading activity involving soybeans, corn, bulk vessels, brokers, foreign suppliers, or jurisdictions viewed by the bank as elevated trade-based-money-laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; commodity descriptions and HS classifications; supplier and customer list; standard sales and purchase contracts; Incoterms; shipping routes; vessel and port information; bills of lading; inspection and quality certificates; customs records; invoices; insurance; sanctions-screening procedure; anti-bribery policy; and documented three-way reconciliation of contract, goods movement, and payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high transaction volumes or mismatch between projected activity and the company's paid-up capital, staffing, premises, or historical accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury forecast; monthly transaction-volume and value estimates; cash-flow model; capitalisation evidence; financing agreements; customer and supplier contracts; warehouse or logistics agreements; staffing and operational evidence; management accounts; and explanation of expected payment corridors and seasonal agricultural cycles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned countries, sanctioned parties, restricted vessels, dual-use goods, unusual intermediaries, or high-risk ports and transit routes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty KYC; beneficial-owner certification; vessel IMO number and screening results; sanctions-screening logs covering EU, UN, UK, and US lists where contractually relevant; end-use and end-destination statements; shipping and customs documents; licence or exemption analysis; escalation records; and a documented refusal process for prohibited transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payments, payments from unrelated group companies, split invoices, circular flows, rapid pass-through of funds, or payments inconsistent with the named contracting party.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Triangular-payment policy; written commercial rationale; group structure chart; intercompany agreements; assignment or payment-direction documents; board approval; invoice-to-contract reconciliation; proof of delivery; source-of-funds evidence; and prior bank approval for exceptional payment routing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of cash, private wallets, unregulated offshore platforms, virtual assets, or personal accounts for corporate trade receipts and disbursements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written prohibition policy; bank-account-only payment controls; payment approval matrix; accounting ledger; reconciliation reports; provider authorisation evidence; and corrective-action records demonstrating that corporate funds are segregated from personal or unregulated channels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent tax residence, missing Spanish identification numbers, unclear permanent establishment position, or inability to establish genuine Spanish business substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish tax-registration evidence; NIF; registered-office and operating-premises documents; lease or service-office agreement; local employee or director information where applicable; management and board records; VAT registration or exemption analysis; tax-residence certificates; and explanation of the Spanish operating model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requested documentary letter of credit, receivables finance, or working-capital facility without adequate collateral, audited information, or verifiable trade history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or management financial statements; borrowing-base schedule; customer and supplier references; executed purchase and sale contracts; collateral and insurance documents; credit-insurance arrangements; trade-cycle analysis; bank references; corporate guarantees where appropriate; and evidence of prior settled transactions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity, capital increases, and shareholder loans through an account held in the SL's legal name at an authorised Spanish bank. Use an originating account in the investor's legal name, not a personal or unrelated third-party account. Include the exact legal name, Spanish NIF, registered address, purpose of payment, and transaction reference. For an equity contribution or capital increase, coordinate the bank certificate of deposit, notarial documentation, shareholder resolutions, public deed, and Registro Mercantil filing where legally required. For a shareholder loan, execute a written loan agreement specifying principal, currency, maturity, interest, repayment mechanics, arm's-length terms, and parties; assess Spanish transfer-pricing, withholding-tax, thin-capitalisation, interest-limitation, and related-party reporting consequences. Retain source-of-funds evidence, audited financial statements or tax records of the investor, board approvals, UBO evidence, and bank confirmations. Spain has no universal statutory foreign-exchange purpose-code system equivalent to certain controlled-currency jurisdictions; banks nevertheless require an accurate payment purpose and may use internal or SEPA/SWIFT classification fields. Do not label a loan as equity, or a commercial receipt as capital, merely to facilitate processing. Reconcile the incoming amount to the corporate ledger and maintain documentary support for at least the applicable Spanish accounting, tax, AML, and banking-retention periods.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within SEPA and bank-to-bank SWIFT or ISO 20022 cross-border transfers for non-SEPA or non-euro settlements. MT103 remains a commonly recognised SWIFT customer-credit-transfer format during the migration to ISO 20022; the servicing bank may instead process the payment using the applicable ISO 20022 pacs.008 message. For agricultural commodity purchases, match the payment to the purchase contract, invoice, Incoterm, beneficiary account, bill of lading or other transport evidence, customs data where relevant, inspection certificate, and sanctions-screening record. Use an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit governed by UCP 600 where counterparty, country, credit, or shipment risk justifies it; specify applicant, beneficiary, amount, currency, expiry, latest shipment date, presentation period, required transport and quality documents, insurance, partial shipment and transshipment rules, and applicable sanctions clauses. Confirm whether the LC is transferable only if expressly structured and permitted by the issuing and confirming banks; avoid assuming that an ordinary LC is transferable. For open-account trade, apply dual approval, beneficiary verification, invoice controls, and segregation of duties. Banks may delay or reject payments because of sanctions, incomplete data, trade-based-money-laundering concerns, correspondent-bank restrictions, or document discrepancies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts with an authorised bank for forecast or committed EUR and foreign-currency trade exposures, subject to a documented hedging policy, exposure evidence, suitability or appropriateness assessment, counterparty limits, and applicable MiFID II and EMIR requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with limited convertibility or restricted delivery, where offered by an authorised EU investment firm or bank and legally available for the relevant currency and customer; settlement is normally by net cash difference and requires clear valuation, collateral, close-out, and counterparty terms.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for recurring funding or multi-currency liquidity exposures, documented under an ISDA Master Agreement or equivalent bank documentation and subject to EMIR reporting, risk-mitigation, collateral, clearing, and risk-management requirements where applicable.

Foreign-exchange options, collars, and participating forwards for asymmetric or uncertain commodity cash flows, subject to product-governance, suitability, premium, valuation, break-cost, and accounting-policy controls.

Natural hedging through matching currency-denominated receipts and payments, currency-specific bank accounts, contractual currency clauses, and timing alignment; this is generally the lowest-documentation alternative but does not remove accounting, tax, sanctions, or liquidity controls.

Mandatory operating controls for all derivatives: board-approved treasury policy; exposure register; hedge designation; counterparty credit limits; independent valuation; confirmation matching; collateral monitoring; authorised-signatory controls; IFRS or Spanish GAAP hedge-accounting analysis; EMIR and transaction-reporting assessment; and prohibition on speculative positions unrelated to identifiable commercial or financing exposures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit at the Mercantile Registry (Cuentas Anuales: balance sheet, income statement, statement of changes in equity, notes, and directors' report); balance of the SL's annual compliance record.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil of the province where the SL has its registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary shareholders' meeting must approve accounts within six months after fiscal year-end; deposited within one month of approval. For 31-Dec year-end: by 31 July the same year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry file closure (no further corporate inscriptions accepted until filing); administrative fines of EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000; long-term failure can initiate registry dissolution procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax annual return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200) with tax book values, adjustments, and loss carryforwards.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days after the sixth month following the tax year-end; for calendar-year SL: 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing recargo of 1% per month up to 20%, plus late payment interest; official notice penalties from 50% to 150% of the tax owed; AEAT enforcement can levy assets but does not strike off the SL.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT recapitulative return (Declaración resumen anual de IVA, Modelo 390).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 30 January following the closed calendar year, together with the fourth-quarter periodic return (Modelo 303) where applicable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 1% per month up to 20% plus late payment interest; administrative penalties are proportional to tax affected; not a company strike-off event.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ultimate beneficial ownership register consistency check (Registro de Titulares Reales) accompanying the annual accounts cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil / Registro de Titulares Reales if ownership movements occurred during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual date: update on every share transfer or control change and must be consistent with the annual accounts deposit; annual reconciliation is carried out at the approval meeting before 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or omitted UBO disclosures attract administrative sanctions under Law 10/2010 (AML) and can block subsequent corporate-registry filings; failure to maintain books also creates director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if, for two consecutive years, the SL meets at least two of: (i) total assets over EUR 2,850,000; (ii) net annual turnover over EUR 5,700,000; (iii) average annual headcount over 50. Audit is likewise mandatory for consolidation groups and regulated entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP: Plan General de Contabilidad (Royal Decree 1514/2007) or SME PGC (Royal Decree 1515/2007); consolidated accounts may apply IFRS as endorsed by the EU; annual accounts are prepared in euros.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain has no standalone annual UBO declaration. The compliance mechanism is: (i) maintain an accurate Libro Registro de Socios; (ii) notarize each share transfer and deposit it at the Registro Mercantil; (iii) update the Registro de Titulares Reales when direct or indirect control or 25% ownership changes; and (iv) reconcile the register with the ownership information contained in the annual accounts before deposit.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors and Appointments (Registro de Administradores)
Inventory and Annual Accounts Book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - 4,500 per year for registered office address, book legalization, annual accounts deposit, and general corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 40,000 for a typical auditable limited company; may exceed USD 40,000 for high-volume commodity-trade audit if full scope is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% standard rate; incentives include accelerated depreciation, R&D tax credits (up to 25% of qualifying expenses), investment tax credits, and sector-specific reliefs

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 - Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, filed electronically through the Agencia Tributaria portal (eFAP or Cl@ve) or SII for VAT if applicable
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 25th day of the fourth month following the end of the fiscal year (e.g. April 25 for calendar year ending 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sum of all income items including sales of goods, services, and other operating revenues from bulk commodity trading
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A for resident entities; non-residents file Modelo 210 with different boxes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, financial costs, and provisions related to trading activities
Net income after deductions, subject to adjustments for transfer pricing and thin cap

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Administrative fines from 100 EUR to 5,000 EUR for late filing; daily surcharge of 0.1% of the tax due, capped at 20% of the tax; criminal sanctions in aggravated cases

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Spanish Tax Agency confirming residency, submit the TRC along with Form 100 or 130 to the withholding agent (e.g. bank or payer), and claim DTA relief by attaching the certificate to the withholding declaration; process via Agencia Tributaria if disputes arise
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 19% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under most DTAs (e.g. 0% with EU countries); Interest: 19% statutory, often reduced to 0% under DTAs if paid on arm's length debt

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 20 million EUR in consolidated group revenue triggers mandatory Master File and Local File documentation
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spanish Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to entities engaged in certain activities; for a bulk commodity trading company, genuine economic substance is required including adequate employees, premises, and core income-generating activities in Spain

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting income from commodity sales or inflating expenses through related party transactions without economic justification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: fines equivalent to 100% of evaded tax, imprisonment from 6 months to 4 years, and confiscation of assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability, disqualification from corporate offices, and civil claims for restitution of damages

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Spanish SL with no real business operations, employees, or assets solely for tax avoidance or repatriation purposes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative dissolution of the company, fines up to 1 million EUR, and potential criminal sanctions for fraudulent incorporation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing of the corporate veil leading to personal liability for tax debts, possible imprisonment for fraudulent acts, and travel bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct due diligence on cross-border payments for grain purchases or suspicious repatriations without proper KYC/AML controls
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines from 300,000 EUR to 1 million EUR or more; possible criminal prosecution under money laundering laws with sentences up to 6 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, disqualification, and joint liability for company fines
